interface.title: EarthSense: Interactive exploration of Global Dimming and Brightening (FORTH-RTM SSR)
interface.field: Atmospheric science / climate science (surface solar radiation, radiative transfer modelling)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring and interpreting finished model output: mapping, validating against ground stations, and attributing trends to drivers
interface.what_it_is_for: Explore modelled global surface solar radiation (SSR) maps and anomalies, check them against GEBA ground stations with evaluation metrics, and attribute SSR dimming/brightening at a pixel or region to aerosol, cloud, water-vapour and ozone drivers and to climate variables.

data.note: This deployment uses small synthetic data (a 7x12 grid and 6 made-up stations) produced by generate_data.py instead of the 930 MB FORTH-RTM/GEBA Zenodo dataset, so the values only show how the tool works. Sign-in was not needed. Downloads during the run: contributions_lon90.0_lat60.0.csv, Climate_timeseries_lon90.0_lat60.0.csv, GDB_Drivers_timeserie_lon90.0_lat60.0.csv and bokeh_plot.png. The landing badges do not match the app names in the repo: 'EarthSense 1' opens /app2_mirror (SSR maps and anomalies), 'EarthSense 2' opens /app3_mirror (station evaluation) and 'EarthSense 3' opens /app1_mirror (drivers and climate). The title and dataset call the model FORTH-RTM; every panel labels it FMC-RTM. This tree uses the panel name FMC-RTM.

tree.general: Describe how a gridded environmental quantity changed over decades, check it against ground measurements, and find which contributing factors explain the change
tree.specific: Map FMC-RTM SSR 1984-2018 and its global dimming/brightening (GDB), evaluate it against GEBA stations, and attribute GDB to aerosol, cloud, H2O and O3 drivers and to climate variables

features.name: Site picker to model-vs-observation evaluation dashboard

click 'model' or 'station' in the time-series legend to hide that line
click another station to compare

read the 'Current position' line and the contribution bars

features.name: Sortable correlation/significance table with colour flags
features.general: A table of each factor's correlation with the target (Pearson, Spearman), its change and its p-value, with strong ones coloured and sortable by any column
features.specific: 'Correlation and Changes of Annual Anomalies' table (Parameters, Pearson_R, Spearman_R, Change, Pval_95) for 18 drivers and climate variables; strong correlations are shown in red and significant p-values in green, and it updates with each pixel or region
steps: select a pixel or region on the GDB map
read the coloured rows
click a column header such as Pval_95 to sort
select another location; the sort is kept
